interfaces.name: package_outline
interfaces.what: LGA-14L body 2.5000 x 3.0000 mm, height 0.8600 mm MAX (0.8300 mm TYP on the datasheet cover p.1 — both are the vendor's own, a typ and a max of the same package; the MAX is carried in body_mm because that is what an enclosure must clear), 14 lands on a 0.5000 mm pitch, each land 0.2500 ±0.05 x 0.4750 ±0.05, the two land rows 1.5000 mm apart, pin 1 indicated on both top and bottom views, seating-plane flatness 0.0500 mm to datum C, general tolerance ±0.1 mm unless otherwise specified, ECOPACK. The frame is the package's geometric centre ON THE SEATING PLANE (z = 0 is the PCB land plane, +z into the body), which is the datum an SMT placement uses. WHAT THIS ROW STILL DOES NOT CLAIM: the land PATTERN to etch on a board — the drawing gives the package's own lands and sends a reader to ST technical note TN0018 for the land pattern, which is a separate document and is not in this folder; and the BOARD this chip sits on, Pollen's imu_to_dxl v2, is unpublished, so how the package is oriented on it is unknown. `accepts` is EMPTY on purpose: an SMT land joint is connection:solder-smt, which is NOT on this shelf — naming it would dangle, and a dangling ref is a FAIL in bin/triad check, never a warning.
interfaces.source: READ OFF THE VENDOR'S OWN MECHANICAL DRAWING: STMicroelectronics LSM6DSV16X datasheet DS13510 Rev 4 (May 2023), section 19.1 'LGA-14L package information', Figure 33 'LGA-14L 2.5 x 3.0 x 0.86 mm package outline and mechanical data', PAGE 175 of 198 — the copy in this folder (../../../datasheet.pdf, sha256 ec53c0e5952fc0c9587ed32b56d066016c2954bc6e9d18355b13a1c4cda17894 in the folder's PROVENANCE.json, re-fetched 2026-09-03 from https://www.st.com/resource/en/datasheet/lsm6dsv16x.pdf and byte-identical), read 2026-09-03 (lane T). SUPERSEDES the row published 2026-09-02, which cited the ST PRODUCT PAGE ('LGA 14L', '2.5 mm x 3 mm x 0.83 mm') and said the land grid was CANNOT DETERMINE because the mechanical drawing was 'NOT on disk in this folder today'. IT WAS ON DISK: the drawing is on page 175 of the datasheet.pdf that PROVENANCE.json already hashed. TWO THINGS CHANGE with the better source. (1) The land grid, previously CANNOT DETERMINE, is measured. (2) body_mm's z is now the drawing's 0.8600 MAX rather than 0.8300. CORRECTION TO THIS ROW'S OWN FIRST WORDING, 2026-09-03: it said the 0.83 'appears nowhere on the drawing and carries no stated basis'. The first half is true; the second is FALSE and is withdrawn. 0.83 is the vendor's own TYP, printed three times in this same PDF — cover p.1 '(2.5 x 3.0 x 0.83 mm) typ.' and 'Compact footprint: 2.5 mm x 3 mm x 0.83 mm', and section 1 p.11 — and ELECTRONICS-DATASHEET.html already carried both figures and said they are the same package read two ways. A typ 0.0300 mm under a max is not an error; carrying the typ as if it were the envelope would be, which is why body_mm holds the max and body_h_typ_mm holds the typ.
interfaces.body_mm_basis: L 2.50 ±0.1, W 3.00 ±0.1, H 0.86 MAX — the three rows of the OUTER DIMENSIONS table inside Figure 33, read verbatim. z here is the drawing's MAXIMUM, which is the figure a clearance check needs. THE VENDOR PUBLISHES TWO HEIGHTS FOR THE SAME PACKAGE AND BOTH ARE ITS OWN: 0.8300 mm TYP on the datasheet COVER, page 1 of 198, verbatim '(2.5 x 3.0 x 0.83 mm) typ.' and 'Compact footprint: 2.5 mm x 3 mm x 0.83 mm', repeated in section 1 p.11 'a small plastic land grid array (LGA) package of 2.5 x 3.0 x 0.83 mm'; and 0.8600 mm MAX in the OUTER DIMENSIONS table of Figure 33, p.175. They do not contradict each other — a typ and a max of one package, 0.0300 mm apart — and ELECTRONICS-DATASHEET.html records both. L and W carry ±0.1, which is also the drawing's stated general tolerance.

land_grid_mm.basis: Figure 33 callouts, verbatim: '0.5' pitch (called twice), '14x 0.25±0.05' and '14x 0.475±0.05' land dimensions, '1.5' between the land rows, '4x (0.1)' as a reference (parenthesised = reference dimension, not toleranced), '0.05 C' flatness to datum C. Pin 1 is indicated on both the TOP VIEW and the BOTTOM VIEW. NOT on this drawing and therefore NOT recorded: the land PATTERN a board should etch — the drawing's own note sends a reader to ST technical note TN0018 for land pattern and soldering, which is a different document and is not in this folder.
